claim: Six translation inhibitors (anisomycin, lycorine, 4E1RCat, salubrinal, homoharringtonine, and amicoumacin C) reduced puromycin incorporation relative to DMSO controls to varying degrees.
source: The six molecules examined all reduced puromycin incorporation relative to DMSO controls to varying degrees (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by western blot data showing reduced puromycin incorporation (Figure 1B) and quantification (Figure 1C).

claim: Anisomycin, lycorine, 4E1RCat, and salubrinal were selected based on their ability to lower the concentration of newly synthesized proteins by approximately 40-50%.
source: Based on their ability to lower the concentration of newly synthesized proteins by ~40–50% and their annotated targets (vide infra), we selected four structurally distinct inhibitors, anisomycin, lycorine, 4E1RCat, and salubrinal, to investigate further (Figure 1D).
evidence: Based on SUnSET assay results showing comparable reductions in protein synthesis.

claim: Anisomycin and lycorine function as translation elongation (TE) inhibitors in C. elegans.
source: As expected for the TE inhibitors, anisomycin and lycorine decreased fluorescence in both green and red channels.
evidence: Demonstrated using bi-cistronic reporter showing reduction of both cap-dependent (GFP) and IRES-dependent (tdTomato) translation (Figure 1F).

claim: 4E1RCat and salubrinal function as translation initiation (TI) inhibitors in C. elegans.
source: On the other hand, the TI inhibitors 4E1RCat and salubrinal only decreased the fluorescence of the green channel, consistent with an initiation-dependent translation of the GFP mRNA sequence and the initiation-independent translation of the IRES-tdTomato sequence (Figure 1F).
evidence: Demonstrated using bi-cistronic reporter showing selective reduction of cap-dependent (GFP) but not IRES-dependent (tdTomato) translation.

claim: All four translation inhibitors (anisomycin, lycorine, 4E1RCat, and salubrinal) significantly improved the survival of N2 animals under thermal stress at 36°C.
source: Hourly monitoring revealed that all four molecules significantly improved the survival of N2 animals (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by thermotolerance assay data showing increased survival at 36°C.

claim: Translation elongation inhibitors (anisomycin and lycorine) protect hsf-1(sy441) mutants from heat stress.
source: Only the TE inhibitors anisomycin and lycorine protected hsf-1(sy441) from HS-induced proteotoxicity, while the TI inhibitors 4E1RCat and salubrinal did not (Figure 2C).
evidence: Demonstrated by thermotolerance assay in hsf-1(sy441) mutants.

claim: Translation initiation inhibitors (4E1RCat and salubrinal) do not protect hsf-1(sy441) mutants from heat stress.
source: Only the TE inhibitors anisomycin and lycorine protected hsf-1(sy441) from HS-induced proteotoxicity, while the TI inhibitors 4E1RCat and salubrinal did not (Figure 2C).
evidence: Demonstrated by thermotolerance assay in hsf-1(sy441) mutants showing no protection.

claim: Pre-treatment with anisomycin suppressed the increase in protein insolubility following a 2 hr heat shock at 36°C in wild-type N2 animals.
source: Furthermore, pre-treatment with the TE inhibitor anisomycin suppressed the increase in protein insolubility (Figure 2D and E), consistent with the observed thermal protection.
evidence: Demonstrated by sequential detergent extraction and quantification of insoluble proteins.

claim: Translation initiation inhibitors trigger an HSR-dependent mechanism to protect from thermal stress.
source: These results reveal that TI inhibitors trigger an HSR-dependent mechanism to protect from thermal stress, while TE inhibitors trigger an HSR-independent mechanism.
evidence: Inferred from the requirement of HSF-1 for TI inhibitor protection but not TE inhibitor protection from heat stress.

claim: Translation elongation inhibitors trigger an HSR-independent mechanism to protect from thermal stress.
source: These results reveal that TI inhibitors trigger an HSR-dependent mechanism to protect from thermal stress, while TE inhibitors trigger an HSR-independent mechanism.
evidence: Inferred from the ability of TE inhibitors to protect hsf-1(sy441) mutants from heat stress.

claim: Following a 2 hr heat shock, the initially diffuse PolyQ::YFP signal gradually localized into puncta in AM140 animals.
source: After a 2 hr HS, the initially diffuse PolyQ signal gradually localized into puncta (Figure 3B, Video 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by live imaging time-lapse microscopy.

claim: Aggregation foci formation resulted from a redistribution of the YFP signal into aggregation foci as the total level of YFP fluorescent signal for a given animal remained constant.
source: Aggregation foci formation resulted from a redistribution of the YFP signal into aggregation foci as the total level of YFP fluorescent signal for a given animal remained constant (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by measuring total YFP fluorescence over time showing no significant change.

claim: Translation elongation inhibitors lycorine and anisomycin significantly reduced heat shock-induced PolyQ aggregation.
source: Only TE inhibitors lycorine and anisomycin significantly reduced HS-induced PolyQ aggregation, while the TI inhibitors 4E1RCat had a small effect and salubrinal had no effect (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by live imaging quantification of PolyQ aggregates.

claim: Translation initiation inhibitor 4E1RCat had a small effect on heat shock-induced PolyQ aggregation.
source: Only TE inhibitors lycorine and anisomycin significantly reduced HS-induced PolyQ aggregation, while the TI inhibitors 4E1RCat had a small effect and salubrinal had no effect (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by live imaging quantification of PolyQ aggregates.

claim: Translation initiation inhibitor salubrinal had no effect on heat shock-induced PolyQ aggregation.
source: Only TE inhibitors lycorine and anisomycin significantly reduced HS-induced PolyQ aggregation, while the TI inhibitors 4E1RCat had a small effect and salubrinal had no effect (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by live imaging quantification of PolyQ aggregates.

claim: Pre-treatment with anisomycin and lycorine reduced the number of PolyQ aggregates per worm but did not change the onset of aggregation, the rate of formation, or the final size of the aggregation foci.
source: Pre-treatment with anisomycin and lycorine reduced the number of PolyQ aggregates per worm. However, pre-treatment did not change the onset of aggregation, the rate of formation, or the final size of the aggregation foci (Morley et al., 2002; Figure 3D).
evidence: Demonstrated by time-lapse imaging analysis of PolyQ aggregation dynamics.

claim: The effect of anisomycin or lycorine on PolyQ aggregation is time-dependent, with strong inhibition following 12 hr preincubation but less so following 4 hr preincubation.
source: Furthermore, we found the effect of anisomycin or lycorine to be time-dependent. They strongly inhibited aggregation following a 12 hr preincubation period but less so following a 4 hr preincubation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Demonstrated by comparing aggregation with different preincubation times.

claim: Starting treatment with anisomycin after the heat shock did not reduce the number of aggregation foci.
source: Starting treatment with anisomycin after the HS did not reduce the number of aggregation foci (not shown).
evidence: Stated as experimental observation without shown data.

claim: Bortezomib decreased the survival of both N2 and hsf-1(sy441) animals.
source: Compared to non-treated controls, bortezomib decreased the survival of both genotypes.
evidence: Demonstrated by survival assay with bortezomib treatment.

claim: Translation elongation inhibitors improved the survival of hsf-1(sy441) animals treated with bortezomib back to untreated levels.
source: TE inhibitors improved the survival of the hsf-1(sy441) animal back to untreated levels but only showed a non-significant tendency to improve the survival of N2 wild-type animals (Figure 4B).
evidence: Demonstrated by survival assay combining TE inhibitors with bortezomib.

claim: Translation elongation inhibitors showed only a non-significant tendency to improve the survival of N2 wild-type animals treated with bortezomib.
source: TE inhibitors improved the survival of the hsf-1(sy441) animal back to untreated levels but only showed a non-significant tendency to improve the survival of N2 wild-type animals (Figure 4B).
evidence: Demonstrated by survival assay combining TE inhibitors with bortezomib.

claim: Translation initiation inhibitors enhanced the proteotoxicity elicited by bortezomib in both N2 and hsf-1(sy441) backgrounds.
source: In contrast, TI inhibitors enhanced the proteotoxicity elicited by bortezomib in both backgrounds.
evidence: Demonstrated by survival assay showing decreased survival with TI inhibitors plus bortezomib.

claim: Bortezomib-treated hsf-1(sy441) animals exhibited a sma (small) phenotype.
source: We also observed bortezomib-treated hsf-1(sy441) animals to shrink in size (sma phenotype) (Figure 4C).
evidence: Demonstrated by visual observation and imaging.

claim: Anisomycin substantially rescued the sma phenotype in bortezomib-treated hsf-1(sy441) animals, almost completely reversing the animals back to normal size.
source: Anisomycin substantially rescued sma phenotypes, almost completely reversing the animals back to normal size (Figure 4D).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantification of worm length at day 3 of adulthood.

claim: Treating PolyQ35::YFP animals with bortezomib caused extensive protein aggregation.
source: As expected, treating PolyQ::YFP animals with bortezomib caused extensive protein aggregation.
evidence: Stated as expected observation in PolyQ animals.

claim: Bortezomib treatment induced the sma phenotype in PolyQ35::YFP transgenic animals, which was almost entirely rescued by anisomycin.
source: As with hsf-1(sy441), bortezomib treatment also induced the sma phenotype in the PolyQ35::YFP transgenic animals, which was almost entirely rescued by anisomycin (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: Demonstrated by measuring worm length at day 5 of adulthood.

claim: Translation elongation inhibitors did not affect proteasome activity in either N2 or hsf-1(sy441) strains.
source: TE inhibitors did not seem to affect proteasome activity in either strain.
evidence: Demonstrated by 20S proteasome activity assay (Figure 4G).

claim: Translation initiation inhibitors reduced N2 proteasome activity compared to DMSO-treated controls.
source: In contrast, TI inhibitors reduced N2 proteasome activity compared to DMSO-treated controls, providing a rationale for their increased toxicity in our proteasome survival assay (Figure 4G).
evidence: Demonstrated by 20S proteasome activity assay.

claim: hsf-1(sy441) mutants showed significantly decreased proteasome activity compared to N2 controls.
source: hsf-1(sy441) mutants showed significantly decreased proteasome activity compared to N2 controls, which was not further reduced by TI inhibitors in hsf-1(sy441).
evidence: Demonstrated by 20S proteasome activity assay (Figure 4G).

claim: Translation initiation inhibitors did not further reduce proteasome activity in hsf-1(sy441) mutants.
source: hsf-1(sy441) mutants showed significantly decreased proteasome activity compared to N2 controls, which was not further reduced by TI inhibitors in hsf-1(sy441).
evidence: Demonstrated by 20S proteasome activity assay (Figure 4G).

claim: Inhibition of translation elongation using anisomycin and lycorine showed no, or only a minor, lifespan extension in N2 animals.
source: Inhibition of translation in wild-type animals using the two TE inhibitors, anisomycin and lycorine, showed no, or only a minor, lifespan extension in N2 animals (Figure 5A).
evidence: Demonstrated by lifespan assays.

claim: Inhibition of translation initiation by 4E1RCat and salubrinal dose-dependently extended lifespan of N2 animals.
source: In contrast, inhibition of TI by the inhibitors 4E1RCat and salubrinal dose-dependently extended lifespan of N2 animals (Figure 5B).
evidence: Demonstrated by lifespan assays at different concentrations.

claim: The difference in the effect on lifespan by translation elongation and translation initiation inhibitors cannot be explained by reducing overall protein synthesis alone.
source: This difference was observed despite all four translation inhibitors reducing protein translation to the same extent (Figure 1B). Thus, the difference in the effect on lifespan by TE and TI inhibitors cannot be explained by reducing overall protein synthesis alone.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that all inhibitors reduce protein synthesis similarly but have different effects on lifespan.

claim: Translation initiation inhibitors 4E1RCat and salubrinal failed to significantly extend lifespan in hsf-1(sy441) mutants.
source: As expected, both 4E1RCat and salubrinal failed to extend lifespan in hsf-1(sy441) mutants significantly.
evidence: Demonstrated by lifespan assays in hsf-1(sy441) mutants.

claim: Inhibition of translation initiation extends lifespan dependent on HSF-1.
source: This result is consistent with genetic work by both the Rodgers and Tavernarakis labs, which showed inhibition of TI extends lifespan dependent on HSF-1 (through ifg-1 and ife-2, respectively) (Howard et al., 2016; Rieckher et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by cited genetic studies and current experimental data.

claim: Treatment with translation elongation inhibitors anisomycin and lycorine significantly extended the lifespan of hsf-1(sy441) mutants by approximately 20%.
source: As Figure 4—figure supplement 1 hinted, treatment with the TE inhibitors anisomycin and lycorine significantly extended the lifespan of hsf-1(sy441) mutants by ~20% (Figure 5B).
evidence: Demonstrated by lifespan assays in hsf-1(sy441) mutants.

claim: The translation elongation inhibitor cycloheximide extended lifespan in hsf-1(sy441) mutants.
source: Similar results were obtained for the TE inhibitor cycloheximide (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by lifespan assays.

claim: Only the two translation initiation inhibitors that extended lifespan caused significant decreases in the amount of SDS-insoluble aggregates in aged N2 animals.
source: We found that only the two TI inhibitors that extended lifespan caused significant decreases in the amount of SDS-insoluble aggregates and that the TE inhibitors failed to do so (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: Demonstrated by sequential detergent extraction of day 8 animals.

claim: Translation elongation inhibitors failed to reduce age-associated protein aggregation in N2 animals.
source: We found that only the two TI inhibitors that extended lifespan caused significant decreases in the amount of SDS-insoluble aggregates and that the TE inhibitors failed to do so (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: Demonstrated by sequential detergent extraction of day 8 animals.

claim: All four translation inhibitors reduced the concentration of newly synthesized proteins in N2 animals.
source: As before, all four inhibitors reduced the concentration of newly synthesized proteins in N2.
evidence: Demonstrated by SUnSET assay (Figure 6A and B).

claim: Translation initiation inhibitors increased the concentration of newly synthesized proteins by 1.5- to 2-fold in hsf-1(sy441) animals.
source: In contrast, TI inhibitors increased the concentration of newly synthesized proteins by 1.5- to 2-fold in the hsf-1(sy441) animals (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Demonstrated by SUnSET assay showing increased puromycin incorporation.

claim: The increased concentration of newly synthesized proteins in hsf-1(sy441) animals treated with translation initiation inhibitors is not due to increased intake of puromycin.
source: We confirmed that this effect is not due to increased intake of puromycin, as inhibitor treatment did not affect food intake (Figure 6C).
evidence: Demonstrated by food intake assay measuring bacterial clearance.

claim: None of the translation inhibitors induced the HSF-1-activated heat shock reporter hsp-16.2::GFP.
source: Furthermore, none of the translation inhibitors induced the HSF-1-activated heat shock reporter hsp-16.2::GFP (Figure 6D).
evidence: Demonstrated by fluorescence assay of hsp-16.2::GFP reporter.

claim: RNAi-mediated knockdown of eIF4G/ifg-1 reduced the concentration of newly synthesized proteins in N2 animals.
source: As seen for 4E1RCat, the knockdown of eIF4G/ifg-1 reduced the protein concentration in N2 but dramatically increased it in hsf-1(sy441) mutants (Figure 6E).
evidence: Demonstrated by SUnSET assay with ifg-1 RNAi.

claim: RNAi-mediated knockdown of eIF4G/ifg-1 dramatically increased the concentration of newly synthesized proteins in hsf-1(sy441) mutants.
source: As seen for 4E1RCat, the knockdown of eIF4G/ifg-1 reduced the protein concentration in N2 but dramatically increased it in hsf-1(sy441) mutants (Figure 6E).
evidence: Demonstrated by SUnSET assay with ifg-1 RNAi.

claim: 4E1RCat treatment significantly extended lifespan in N2 animals.
source: As we previously observed (Figure 5A and B) 4E1RCat treatment of N2 animals significantly extended lifespan (Figure 6F).
evidence: Demonstrated by lifespan assay.

claim: 4E1RCat treatment did not extend lifespan in ifg-1(cxTi9279) animals.
source: However, no lifespan extension was observed in ifg-1(cxTi9279) animals (Figure 6G), showing that 4E1RCat extends lifespan by on-target action.
evidence: Demonstrated by lifespan assay in ifg-1 mutants.

claim: 4E1RCat extends lifespan by on-target action on eIF4G/ifg-1.
source: However, no lifespan extension was observed in ifg-1(cxTi9279) animals (Figure 6G), showing that 4E1RCat extends lifespan by on-target action.
evidence: Inferred from lack of lifespan extension in ifg-1 mutants.

claim: Inhibition of eIF4G/ifg-1 requires HSF-1 to lower the concentration of newly synthesized proteins.
source: Therefore, we concluded that inhibition of eIF4G/ifg-1 requires HSF-1 to lower the concentration of newly synthesized proteins.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that ifg-1 inhibition increases protein synthesis in hsf-1 mutants.

claim: The beneficial effects of 4E1RCat treatment are not observed in hsf-1(sy441) mutants because inhibition of eIF4G/ifg-1 fails to lower protein concentrations in this strain.
source: Consequently, the beneficial effects of 4E1RCat treatment are not observed in hsf-1(sy441) mutants as inhibition of eIF4G/ifg-1 fails to lower protein concentrations in this strain.
evidence: Inferred from the combined observations of increased protein synthesis and lack of beneficial effects in hsf-1 mutants.

claim: Inhibition of translation elongation rescues proteostasis in animals with pre-existing proteotoxicities such as a compromised heat shock response, reduced proteasome activity, or the expression of aggregation-prone proteins.
source: Overall, TE inhibition effectively rescued proteostasis in animals with pre-existing proteotoxicities, such as a compromised HSR, reduced proteasome activity, or the expression of aggregation-prone proteins.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing TE inhibitor protection in compromised backgrounds.

claim: Inhibition of translation initiation did little to rescue pre-existing proteotoxicity or worsened it but proved effective at preventing emerging proteotoxicity with age.
source: Conversely, inhibition of TI did little to rescue pre-existing proteotoxicity or worsen it but proved effective at preventing emerging proteotoxicity, for example, with age.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing TI inhibitor effects on different proteotoxic conditions.

claim: Inhibition of translation initiation or elongation has distinct consequences for proteostasis and their mechanisms to control the concentration of newly synthesized proteins can be genetically separated.
source: Overall, our findings establish that inhibition of TI or TE has distinct consequences for proteostasis and that their mechanisms to control the concentration of newly synthesized proteins can be genetically separated.
evidence: Inferred from the totality of experimental results showing differential effects.

claim: The increased mortality observed after combining bortezomib with translation initiation inhibitors is likely to be the result of the lower expression of HSP90/daf-21 and HSP70/hsp-1, whose translation depends on eIF4G/ifg-1, and the ability of both treatments to lower proteasome activity independently.
source: The increased mortality observed after combining bortezomib with TI inhibitors is likely to be the result of the lower expression of HSP90/daf-21 and HSP70/hsp-1, whose translation depends on eIF4G/ifg-1 (Rogers et al., 2011) and the ability of both treatments to lower proteasome activity independently (Figure 4).
evidence: Speculative explanation based on known dependencies and observed proteasome activity.

claim: The lower proteasome activity induced by translation initiation inhibitors is likely to enhance the proteotoxicity of bortezomib.
source: The lower proteasome activity induced by the TI inhibitors is likely to enhance the proteotoxicity of bortezomib.
evidence: Speculative explanation based on observed proteasome activity data.

claim: Long-term inhibition of translation initiation or elongation differentially affects proteasomal activity and its proteotoxic effects.
source: Thus, long-term inhibition of TI or TE differentially affects proteasomal activity and its proteotoxic effects.
evidence: Inferred from differential effects on proteasome activity and proteotoxicity.

claim: HSF-1 or one of its targets is necessary for the translation initiation machinery to control protein synthesis.
source: This initial model is still likely valid, but our study shows that HSF-1 has a more immediate role. HSF-1, or one of its targets, is necessary for the TI machinery to control protein synthesis.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that TI inhibition increases protein synthesis in hsf-1 mutants.

claim: Selective translation can only occur if translation initiation itself is inhibited.
source: Selective translation can only occur if TI itself is inhibited.
evidence: Logical inference from the mechanism of selective translation.

claim: HSF-1 activity directly or indirectly modulates the ability of translation initiation components to control the concentration of newly synthesized proteins.
source: Hence, HSF-1 activity directly or indirectly modulates the ability of TI components to control the concentration of newly synthesized proteins.
evidence: Inferred from the requirement of HSF-1 for TI inhibitors to reduce protein synthesis.

claim: Lowering the concentration of newly synthesized proteins is necessary for the beneficial effects of translation initiation inhibitors.
source: The inability of TI inhibitors to reduce the concentration of newly synthesized proteins in hsf-1(sy441) mutants and the inability to extend their lifespan shows that lowering the concentration of newly synthesized proteins is necessary for the beneficial effects.
evidence: Inferred from the correlation between inability to reduce protein synthesis and lack of beneficial effects.

claim: Lowering the concentration of newly synthesized proteins is sufficient to protect from proteotoxic stress but is not sufficient to extend lifespan in wild-type animals.
source: On the other hand, the finding that TE inhibitors protect from proteotoxic stress but do not extend lifespan shows that lowering the concentration of newly synthesized proteins is sufficient to protect from proteotoxic stress but is not sufficient to extend lifespan in wild-type, which appears to require selective translation.
evidence: Inferred from the differential effects of TE inhibitors on proteotoxicity versus lifespan.

claim: Extension of lifespan in wild-type animals appears to require selective translation.
source: On the other hand, the finding that TE inhibitors protect from proteotoxic stress but do not extend lifespan shows that lowering the concentration of newly synthesized proteins is sufficient to protect from proteotoxic stress but is not sufficient to extend lifespan in wild-type, which appears to require selective translation.
evidence: Inferred from the requirement of TI inhibition (which enables selective translation) for lifespan extension.

claim: The lack of HSF-1 abolishes the ability of ifg-1 RNAi to lower the concentration of newly synthesized proteins.
source: Our results provide a compelling explanation for their findings, in that the lack of HSF-1 abolishes the ability of ifg-1 RNAi to lower the concentration of newly synthesized proteins and thus the protection from tunicamycin toxicity.
evidence: Inferred from current experimental results and cited previous findings (Howard et al., 2016).

claim: Cycloheximide unreliably reduces puromycin incorporation relative to DMSO control in N2 animals.
source: Cycloheximide (100 μΜ) unreliably reduces puromycin incorporation relative to DMSO control in N2 animals. All three experiments were conducted under identical conditions and run on the same blot to reduce technical batch effects but resulted in unreliable reductions of newly synthesized proteins.
evidence: Demonstrated by SUnSET assay showing variable results (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).

claim: Cycloheximide functions as a translation elongation inhibitor in C. elegans.
source: Using the SUnSET assay and our bi-cistronic reporter, we show that cycloheximide directly reduces the concentration of newly synthesized proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B) and functions as a TE inhibitor since we observed a reduction of both the GFP and the tdTomato signal.
evidence: Demonstrated by bi-cistronic reporter showing reduction of both cap-dependent and IRES-dependent translation.

claim: The inhibition of translation by cycloheximide across different trials was considerably more variable compared to anisomycin and lycorine.
source: We noted that the inhibition of translation by cycloheximide across different trials was considerably more variable compared to anisomycin and lycorine (compare Figure 1B and C with Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Demonstrated by comparing variability in SUnSET assay results.

claim: Anisomycin and lycorine reliably reduced the concentration of newly synthesized proteins by 40-50%.
source: We therefore decided to proceed with anisomycin and lycorine as TE inhibitors as they reliably reduced the concentration of newly synthesized proteins by 40–50%.
evidence: Demonstrated by consistent SUnSET assay results.

claim: Protein synthesis largely determines the folding load on the proteostasis network.
source: Protein synthesis largely determines the folding load on the proteostasis network, which regulates protein production, folding, trafficking, and degradation to maintain a functional proteome.
evidence: Statement based on established understanding of proteostasis.

claim: The imbalance of the proteostasis network caused by age-associated stress or acute environmental insults leads to misfolding of proteins, accumulation of aggregates, and eventually to disease.
source: The imbalance of the proteostasis network caused by age-associated stress or acute environmental insults leads to misfolding of proteins, accumulation of aggregates, and eventually to disease (Balch et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by cited reference on proteostasis.

claim: In mice, point mutations in specific tRNAs or components of the ribosomal quality control pathway can lead to protein aggregation and neurodegeneration.
source: For example, in mice, point mutations in specific tRNAs or components of the ribosomal quality control pathway can lead to protein aggregation and neurodegeneration (Vo et al., 2018; Yonashiro et al., 2016; Chu et al., 2009; Nollen et al., 2004; Nedialkova and Leidel, 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references.

claim: Early RNAi screens in C. elegans identified several ribosomal subunits whose knockdown increased the aggregation of polyglutamine proteins.
source: Similarly, early RNAi screens in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans identified several ribosomal subunits whose knockdown increased the aggregation of polyglutamine (PolyQ) proteins (Nollen et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: RNAi-mediated knockdown of translation initiation factors increases lifespan, improves proteostasis, and reduces protein aggregation in C. elegans.
source: For example, RNAi-mediated knockdown of translation initiation factors increases lifespan, improves proteostasis, and reduces protein aggregation in C. elegans (Balch et al., 2008; Rogers et al., 2011; McQuary et al., 2016; Lan et al., 2019; Howard et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of translation prior to a heat shock prevents proteins from aggregating in yeast and cell culture.
source: Similarly, work in yeast and cell culture shows that pharmacological inhibition of translation prior to a heat shock prevents proteins from aggregating (Medicherla and Goldberg, 2008; Choe et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2016; Riback et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references.

claim: In the selective translation model, the increased availability of ribosomes leads to differential translation of mRNAs coding for stress response factors and thus to increased folding capacity.
source: In the selective translation model, the increased availability of ribosomes leads to differential translation of mRNAs coding for stress response factors and thus to increased folding capacity (Rogers et al., 2011; McQuary et al., 2016; Lan et al., 2019; Seo et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references describing the selective translation model.

claim: Studies proposing a version of the selective translation model show that inhibiting translation requires HSF-1 to reduce protein aggregation.
source: In general, studies proposing a version of the selective translation model show that inhibiting translation requires HSF-1 to reduce protein aggregation (Howard et al., 2016; Tye and Churchman, 2021).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: In the reduced folding load model, newly synthesized proteins are the primary aggregation-prone species of proteins.
source: The second model, referred to as the reduced folding load model, proposes that newly synthesized proteins are the primary aggregation-prone species of proteins.
evidence: Description of the reduced folding load model.

claim: In the reduced folding load model, newly synthesized proteins constitute the most significant folding load on the proteostasis machinery.
source: Therefore, newly synthesized proteins constitute the most significant folding load on the proteostasis machinery.
evidence: Logical consequence of the reduced folding load model.

claim: The reduced folding load model does not depend on specific factors but generates folding capacity by reducing the overall folding load.
source: In contrast to the selective translation model, which proposes selective protein synthesis of HSF-1-dependent stress response factors, the reduced folding load model does not depend on specific factors but generates folding capacity by reducing the overall folding load.
evidence: Comparison of the two models.

claim: Previous studies did not control how much protein synthesis was reduced by different modes of translation inhibition making direct comparisons between the selective translation model and the reduced folding load model difficult.
source: Furthermore, previous studies did not control how much protein synthesis was reduced by different modes of translation inhibition making direct comparisons between the selective translation model and the reduced folding load model difficult.
evidence: Critique of previous studies identifying a gap in the literature.

claim: The HSF-1 pathway is not only a downstream target of translation but also directly cooperates with the translation initiation machinery to control the concentration of newly synthesized proteins to restore proteostasis.
source: Our findings suggest that the HSF-1 pathway is not only a downstream target of translation but also directly cooperates with the translation initiation machinery to control the concentration of newly synthesized proteins to restore proteostasis.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that TI inhibition requires HSF-1 to reduce protein synthesis.

claim: Lowering translation is an established mechanism to extend lifespan and delay aging.
source: Lowering translation is an established mechanism to extend lifespan and delay aging (Steffen and Dillin, 2016; Anisimova et al., 2018; Klaips et al., 2018; Hansen et al., 2007; Pan et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references.

claim: Aging is a well-known driver of protein aggregation.
source: Furthermore, aging is a well-known driver of protein aggregation.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge.

claim: Work in cancer cells showed inhibition of translation to block HSF-1 binding to DNA and to specifically reduce the expression of HSP70 and DNAJA chaperones.
source: In contrast, work in cancer cells showed inhibition of translation to block HSF-1 binding to DNA and to specifically reduce the expression of HSP70 and DNAJA chaperones (Santagata et al., 2013), making it difficult to envision how HSF-1 could act as a downstream effector of TI.
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Anisomycin and cycloheximide have previously been reported to extend lifespan in wild type animals.
source: Notably, both anisomycin and cycloheximide have previously been reported to extend lifespan in wild type animals (Tarkhov et al., 2019; Takauji et al., 2016) but these studies were conducted in either non-fully reproductive adults or the exact conditions were not specified (i.e. temperature, whether OP50 feeding bacteria was alive/dead and developmental stage; Takauji et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by cited references with noted caveats about experimental conditions.

claim: Short-term inhibition of translation increases proteasome activity.
source: The lowered proteasome activity observed upon inhibition of TI was surprising as the short-term inhibition of translation increases proteasome activity (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.
